newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to offer second bite at oil contracts.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to offer second bite at oil contracts.

text.p: Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) plans to reoffer three contracts to operate marginal oilfields and two profit-sharing exploration contracts before the end of this year, senior PDVSA sources said on Wednesday.

Contracts to operate the Mata, Cretacico and Bachaquero fields were first offered in the third round of operating licences in June, and would be reoffered between August and October this year, said PDVSA exploration manager Juan Szabo.
The new auction would be run on the same lines as the third round, and the same list of qualified companies would be used.

Szabo said the lack of interest in the Crectacico and Bachaquero fields was due to the large number of other fields available in the third round, and they could attract more interest offered on their own.
The Mata contract was originally won by a Venezuelan consortium of PBE trading and Pivensa, but it was disqualified after PBE Trading was bought out by Marshall.
Separately, Szabo said PDVSA would reoffer profit-sharing exploration contracts for the Sombrero and Catatumbo blocks before the end of the year.
These two blocks failed to receive bids in an auction last year, but Szabo said he hoped to offer companies a better deal this time, with less minimum investment in the Catatumbo block.
He expected more interest in the the Sombrero block since domestic natural gas prices have risen recently and this block was thought to contain mostly gas.
